node_definition.done_when: The repair hold reason reuses the clause composition _no_review_lane_reason already performs (exclusions from review routing, backends whose declared launch is IN_HARNESS_LAUNCH, the previously dropped lane), generalised over the run kind rather than copied, and the review hold's wording is unchanged. A new tests/test_a_repair_hold_names_its_cause.py drives dispatch_repair_for_run on a configuration whose only backend launches in-harness and asserts the run is held with awaiting_lane true, no repair pointer is created, and the reason carries IN_HARNESS_LAUNCH and that backend's name; a second case with a review_excluded_backends entry asserts the exclusion is named. The named negative control (restore the bare repair reason) reddens the in-harness case. The gate is these files, run at base and at head: tests/test_a_repair_hold_names_its_cause.py, tests/test_a_review_never_runs_in_harness.py, tests/test_reflex_dispatches_one_repair.py, tests/test_review_findings_compose_a_repair.py, tests/test_review_reflex_sweep.py, tests/test_review_lane_follows_its_run.py, tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder; each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id outside this fence means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed paths report no finding the base did not. Basetemps and scratch trees go under /tmp in a directory named for this run and are deleted before status complete, printed and listed in artifacts. An evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/a-review-dies-where-nobody-is-looking/a-repair-hold-names-its-cause.html records the change. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
